title: Book notes
audience: For readers who want to remember more than the cover a year later.
description: Book notes your AI organizes: send highlights as you read, and it keeps the quotes, the big idea and what you'll do differently.
note:
Book notes

What stuck from each book: the big idea, the lines worth keeping, and what you'll do differently. Newest book first.

## Books

prompt.default: Use my Amber Notes note "Book notes". When I start a book, add a heading for it at the start of "Books" with append_to_note (at_start), like "### Title by Author". As I send you highlights and thoughts, add them under that book's heading with append_to_note: quotes as > quotes with the page number, my own thoughts as bullets. Keep my words; don't polish them. When I say I've finished, add "**The big idea:**" in three sentences and two to four things I'll do differently as a checklist.

asks: Starting Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman.
Page 31: "The day will never arrive when you finally have everything under control."
I finished it. Wrap it up.

args.text: ### Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman

args.under_heading: Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
args.text:
> "The day will never arrive when you finally have everything under control." (p. 31)

- The to-do list is infinite by design. Finishing it isn't the goal.
- Pick your three big projects; everything else waits.

**The big idea:** life is short and attention is finite. Trying to do everything guarantees the important things get squeezed. Choose what to neglect, on purpose.

- [ ] Keep a list of three active projects, no more
- [ ] Do the most important thing first, before email
